In 2.1, 2.4, 3.3, 3.4 and 4.1 he is a gaunt older man: narrow chest, thin arms, a hollow-cheeked face, long straggly dark hair streaked with grey and a long ragged grey beard. In page-04 4.5, at about x 1137-1443, y 1886-2538 in the original pixels, he is a different body type. He has broad, heavily muscled shoulders and arms and a clearly cut six-pack. His hair is short, tightly curled and mostly grey, ending at the nape. His beard is a fuller, neater white beard. His face is shown in profile and looks younger and heavier-boned. The 4.5 figure should be redrawn gaunt, with long straggly grey-streaked hair and a ragged beard, to match 2.4, 3.3 and 4.1.

1. **The bible allows it.** CONTINUITY.md gives Ibrahim this row for chapters 4 and 5: "Pale vest over a white mundu, no coat." For chapters 6 to 28 it gives "Short coat over a vest with bulging pockets." So the vest under the coat is the same garment in every chapter.

2. **The approved sheet shows the same vest.** On the sheet (concepts/09-ibrahim-marakkar-v15.png), Ibrahim wears a cream vest with a buttoned front and flap pockets, and a "BULGING VEST POCKETS" detail callout. A cream collar shows at his throat in the 3/4 view and in every expression head. The dark muted-teal short coat goes over all of that.

3. **The render is the sheet with the coat taken off.** In page 6, panel 6.5 (crop around x 880 to 1340, y 1740 to 2500 at full size), he wears the same pale buttoned vest with flap pockets and a cream undershirt with a small collar and rolled sleeves. Under it are a white mundu, a white turban, a short grey-flecked beard and a striped shoulder cloth. That is exactly "pale vest over a white mundu, no coat."

4. **The script does not rule out an undershirt.** It never asks for bare arms. "Pale vest over a white mundu" is satisfied here.

5. **It cannot be mistaken for the chapter 6 coat.** The coat is dark teal. Everything on his upper body here is cream, so the coat is not foreshadowed or confused.

6. **No period problem worth flagging.** A buttoned vest with flap pockets is the approved design, not something new in this panel.

Nothing here needs changing.

minors.description: The Young Fisherman's facial hair is not held. Per the script it is a thin black beard, as in 2.4 and 4.1, but 5.4 (and 4.5) give him a full dense black beard covering the jaw, while 6.4 and 6.5 show only a thin moustache over a clean chin. Across pages 5 and 6 he reads as different young men.
minors.evidence: page-05.png 5.4, right-hand figure in the headband, full beard at about (1318-1609, 1637-1859) original px. page-06.png 6.5, Young Fisherman behind Ibrahim, moustache only and clean chin, at about (1262-1401, 1803-1942).

minors.description: The Woman drifts after her introduction. In 5.4 she matches the script: heavy-set, round-faced, in her fifties, hair almost entirely grey. In 5.5, and especially 6.1, she is slimmer, sharper-featured and younger-looking, with mostly black curly hair and only a grey streak. In 6.1 this moves her toward Padmini's sheet (dark curly hair, lean intense face), the matron the script says she must be told apart from.
minors.evidence: page-05.png 5.4, Woman's head at about (957-1248, 1470-1803) original px: grey hair, full round face. page-06.png 6.1, Woman at about (194-444, 541-832): dark curly hair with a grey streak, slim face. page-05.png 5.5, Woman at about (1165-1685, 2100-2540): thinner face, darker hair.

minors.description: The Fisherman's age and hair colour drift. In 2.1, 2.2, 4.2, 5.1 to 5.3 and 6.5 he has black curly hair and a grizzled short beard, a man in his forties. In 3.4, 3.5, 6.1 and 6.2 his hair turns grey and wild and he reads as nearer sixty. That brings him close to the Wary Fisherman's look (grey hair, grey beard). It blurs the two older men in 3.5, where the off-panel Wary balloon sits right over his head, and in 6.2, where the Wary Fisherman is meant to be absent.

In 2.4, 3.1, 4.1, 4.2, 5.3, 6.2, 6.3 and 6.5 it is correctly on his left.

In 4.5 the net is on his right shoulder and the brown cloth on his left. Across the chapter, 2.4, 4.1 and 5.1 use one arrangement and 3.3, 3.4 and 4.5 the other.

Page 3, 3.3 and 3.4: net on his right shoulder.

minors.description: The wreck changes design and position. In 4.1 it is a huge ornate high-sided hull with no masts at all, sitting just beyond the rocks behind the group. Elsewhere it is a dismasted ship with broken masts still standing, out on a reef: 2.4 and 5.1, plus 3.3 as a low hull with masts and no visible stern castle. In 3.5 a large ribbed wreck stands right behind the Fisherman and Nagoji, although 3.3 on the same page puts the wreck far offshore.
minors.evidence: Page 4 r12, panel 4.1 top-left background: a giant carved stern castle with no masts, close inshore. Page 2, 2.4 right background: angled broken masts and rigging on a reef. Page 3, 3.3: a distant low hull with masts. Page 3, 3.5 right background: tall broken hull ribs a few metres behind the men. Page 5, 5.1: a small masted wreck far off.

minors.description: The rope loops are already gone from Nagoji's chest in 2.3, but the script has the Young Fisherman cut them away on camera in 2.4, where they lie freshly cut beside him. In 2.2 rope is still visible at his chest.
minors.evidence: Page 2 r12, 2.3 (water pot close-up): the open tunic and bare chest show only rope burns, with no rope. 2.2: rope coils visible at Nagoji's chest, bottom centre. 2.4: the cut loops lie on the sand.

minors.description: The lighting breaks continuity. 1.4 is a golden sunset with sunbeams bursting through the clouds, but 1.1 on the same page and every beach panel on pages 2 to 4 are flat, grey, storm-overcast daylight (2.1: 'lowering grey sky'). The village pages that follow are also in grey daylight, not dusk.
minors.evidence: Page 1 r12, 1.4 (bottom strip): an orange sun low over the sea with crepuscular rays and gold reflections on wet sand. Page 2, 2.1: a uniform grey overcast sky.

minors.description: Ibrahim reads as taller than the fishermen. The bible says he is 'shorter than the fishermen but broader', and the script wants the Young Fisherman 'half a head taller' just behind him. The Young Fisherman's and the Fisherman's heads sit clearly below Ibrahim's, and he does not read broader. This is his introduction, so it sets his scale for chapters 5 and 6.
minors.evidence: Page 6 r12, 6.5: Ibrahim's turban top is near the panel's top border and his eyes are above the Young Fisherman's headband line. The two fishermen stand behind him with their heads lower.

minors.description: The Fisherman's white shoulder cloth now has a pale blue striped border that matches Ibrahim's towel, where it was plain white everywhere earlier. His face also drifts: it is leaner, with a darker, blacker beard, not the broad face and short grizzled grey beard set in 2.1.
minors.evidence: Page 6 r12, 6.5 right figure (red lungi): blue stripes and fringe at the cloth's end, and a dark beard. Page 2, 2.1 left face: broad face, grey-grizzled beard. Pages 3 to 5: plain white cloth.

minors.description: Anachronistic child's clothing. The girl in the doorway wears a stitched, short-sleeved shirt-blouse over a pleated maroon skirt, a modern frock or pavada look rather than 1740s Kerala draped cotton. She also wears different clothes from the girl in 5.2, who should be the same child.
minors.evidence: A 4x crop of the doorway at the left of 5.3 (about x=210 to 280, y=780 to 890 in display coordinates) shows a beige button-less stitched shirt with set-in sleeves and a gathered maroon skirt.

minors.description: The background village houses have fired clay tile roofs. The script calls for palm-thatch roofs. In a 1740s Travancore fishing hamlet, tiled roofs on commoners' houses are anachronistic, because tiles were reserved for temples, palaces and high-status houses until the 19th century.
minors.evidence: A 3x crop of the upper right background of 5.2 shows two houses behind the palms with ridged rows of clay roof tiles. Only the foreground eaves on the left and right are thatched.

minors.description: The Fisherman's three balloons each have their own tail, and two of the tails stab into his chest rather than his mouth. The second balloon, '<You think leaving one marata on the sand will satisfy either of them?>', is parked directly under Nagoji's face over his chest. The third, '<We might as well gain something.>', is staggered lower-left, so it competes for the second read. Linked balloons (connectors) from one tail at the Fisherman's head, kept off Nagoji, would read cleanly.

minors.description: The framing and the pose differ from the beat. The script asks for a ground-level, tight shot of the hands dug into the grit. The art is a medium shot of Nagoji up on all fours, pushing his torso clear of the surf, with his moustache, chin and ear stud showing. This strong crawl sits between two panels where he lies face down (1.1, then 1.3 with his cheek on the sand), so the sequence reads as up, then down again, which undercuts "limbs ... of lead". The bandages also wrap the whole palm, so the bare, rope-burned heels of the palms the script asks for do not show.
minors.evidence: Page 1, 1.2: full arms, torso, rope across the chest, dhoti and lower face are all in frame. Panel 1.3 directly below shows him prone, cheek pressed to the sand.

minors.description: The time-of-day jump goes the wrong way. The script asks only that the light has shifted, but the art shows a golden sunset with sunbeams. Every following panel (2.1's "lowering grey sky" through the village scenes) is flat grey storm daylight, so the chapter appears to go from evening back to overcast midday.
minors.evidence: Page 1, 1.4: a sunburst through the clouds at top left and orange reflections on the wet sand. Page 2, 2.1 and 2.4 are uniformly grey and overcast.

minors.description: The order of the carry party is reversed. The script has the Wary Fisherman leading the climb. The art puts him last, below and behind the Young Fisherman, while the Fisherman carrying the shoulders is at the front.
minors.evidence: Page 5, 5.1: left to right, the Fisherman (red lungi, holding the shoulders), Nagoji, the Young Fisherman (holding the legs), then the Wary Fisherman with the net, lower right and trailing.

minors.description: The staging drifts from the frozen-moment beat. Nagoji has been set down and slumps against something, not held between the carriers. The Fisherman kneels on the far side of Nagoji, not beside the Woman. The brand is only a small pale patch near the elbow of an arm lying in his lap, so her gaze "fixed on the brand" reads as a look down at his chest.

minors.description: Nagoji's pose contradicts the panels on either side. The Fisherman has just told him to rest, and in 6.3 and 6.5 he lies on the mat. Here he sits bolt upright, cross-legged, in a meditation pose. His chest also shows a single long, healed horizontal scar instead of the raw rope burns drawn in 5.4 and 5.5.
minors.evidence: Page 6, 6.4: Nagoji sits upright and cross-legged with his hands on his knees and eyes closed. There is a thin horizontal scar across the pectorals at about y~1100. In 6.5 directly below, he reclines on a bolster.
